CHAPTER 18 — कर्तव्यनिष्ठा (KARTAVYANISHTHA: Devotion to Duty)

Introduction — कर्तव्यनिष्ठा किम्?

The word कर्तव्यनिष्ठा (kartavya-nistha) is made of two parts: कर्तव्यम् (kartavyam = 'that which ought to be done', one's duty or responsibility) and निष्ठा (nistha = firm devotion, steadfastness, dedication). कर्तव्यनिष्ठा therefore means steadfast devotion to one's duty — doing sincerely, honestly and completely whatever task falls to us, whether or not any reward or praise follows. In Sanskrit tradition this idea is expressed by the great word कर्मयोगः (the yoga of action): work done as an offering, with full effort but without craving for its fruit. In this lesson (NIOS Secondary Sanskrit, Course 209) we read a short story of a dutiful watchman, study its शब्दार्थ (word meanings) and English translation, draw out its moral, learn four famous public-domain verses on कर्म (action) and कर्तव्य (duty), and use them to practise a little Sanskrit grammar (व्याकरणम्).

Why कर्तव्यनिष्ठा matters (कर्तव्यनिष्ठायाः महत्त्वम्)

Every person — a student, a farmer, a soldier, a teacher, a parent — has some कर्तव्य (duty). Society runs smoothly only when each person does his or her own duty faithfully. A guard who abandons his post, a student who neglects study, a doctor who ignores a patient — each causes harm far beyond himself. The person of कर्तव्यनिष्ठा, by contrast, becomes trustworthy (विश्वसनीयः), respected (माननीयः) and inwardly peaceful, because a clear conscience follows honest work. The Bhagavadgita teaches that we have a right only to our action, never to its fruit (कर्मण्येवाधिकारस्ते मा फलेषु कदाचन). This does not mean we should not care about results; it means we should give our whole effort to the duty itself and not be paralysed by greed or fear about the outcome. सत्यम् (truthfulness) and उत्तरदायित्वम् (responsibility) are the two wings of कर्तव्यनिष्ठा: we must be honest about what our duty is, and we must own the results of doing or not doing it.

कथा — कर्तव्यनिष्ठः प्रहरी (The Dutiful Watchman)

(Simple Sanskrit prose — an original retelling.)

एकस्मिन् नगरे धर्मपालः नाम प्रहरी आसीत्। सः राजभवनस्य द्वारपालः आसीत्। प्रतिदिनं निशायां सः द्वारे सावधानः तिष्ठति स्म। एकदा घोरा वृष्टिः अभवत्, प्रबलः वातः च ववौ। शीतेन सर्वे जनाः गृहेषु सुप्ताः। तथापि धर्मपालः स्वस्थानं न अत्यजत्। सः अचिन्तयत् — "मम कर्तव्यं राजभवनस्य रक्षणम्। यदि अहं स्थानं त्यजामि, तर्हि चोराः प्रविशेयुः। कर्तव्यात् महत्तरम् अन्यत् न अस्ति।" तस्यां रात्रौ राजा स्वयं गुप्तवेषेण द्वारम् आगच्छत्। सः अपृच्छत् — "भो प्रहरिन्, किमर्थं त्वम् एवं वृष्टौ शीते च अत्र तिष्ठसि? गृहं गच्छ, विश्रामं कुरु।" धर्मपालः विनयेन अवदत् — "देव, इदं मम कर्तव्यम्। कर्तव्यपालनम् एव मम धर्मः। न अहं सुखाय, न अहं पुरस्काराय अत्र तिष्ठामि; कर्म एव मे कर्तव्यम्।" राजा तस्य वचनेन तस्य कर्तव्यनिष्ठया च अतीव प्रसन्नः अभवत्। प्रातःकाले सः धर्मपालम् आहूय बहुभिः रत्नैः धनेन च तम् अपूजयत्। किन्तु धर्मपालः नम्रः सन् अवदत् — "राजन्, अहं फलम् इच्छन् कर्म न करोमि। कर्म एव मम आनन्दः। तथापि भवतः प्रसादः मम शिरसि।" राजा सभायाम् अवदत् — "एषः एव सत्यः कर्मयोगी। यः फलम् अनपेक्ष्य स्वकर्तव्यं करोति, सः एव धन्यः।"

शब्दार्थ (Word meanings): प्रहरी = watchman, sentinel; द्वारपालः = gatekeeper; राजभवनम् = the royal palace; निशायाम् = at night (सप्तमी); सावधानः = alert, careful; घोरा वृष्टिः = a terrible rain; प्रबलः वातः = a strong wind; ववौ = blew (from वा); सुप्ताः = asleep; स्वस्थानम् = one's own post/place; न अत्यजत् = did not abandon; रक्षणम् = protection, guarding; चोराः = thieves; प्रविशेयुः = might enter; महत्तरम् = greater; गुप्तवेषेण = in disguise (तृतीया); किमर्थम् = why, for what purpose; विश्रामम् = rest; विनयेन = humbly; कर्तव्यपालनम् = the doing/discharge of duty; पुरस्काराय = for reward (चतुर्थी, 'for'); प्रसन्नः = pleased; आहूय = having called; रत्नैः = with jewels; अपूजयत् = honoured; नम्रः = humble; फलम् अनपेक्ष्य = without expecting reward; धन्यः = blessed, fortunate; कर्मयोगी = one devoted to selfless action.

Translation: In a certain city there was a watchman named Dharmapala. He was the gatekeeper of the royal palace. Every night he stood alert at the gate. One day a terrible rain fell and a strong wind blew. In the cold everyone slept in their houses; yet Dharmapala did not leave his post. He thought, 'My duty is the protection of the palace. If I leave my place, thieves may enter. There is nothing greater than duty.' That night the king himself came to the gate in disguise and asked, 'O watchman, why do you stand here in such rain and cold? Go home and rest.' Dharmapala said humbly, 'Sire, this is my duty. Doing my duty is my dharma. I stand here neither for comfort nor for reward; action itself is my duty.' The king was greatly pleased by his words and his devotion to duty. In the morning he called Dharmapala and honoured him with many jewels and wealth. But Dharmapala said modestly, 'O king, I do not act desiring reward. The work itself is my joy. Yet your grace is upon my head.' In the assembly the king declared, 'This is a true karma-yogi. He who does his own duty without looking to its fruit — he alone is blessed.'

Moral (सारः): कर्तव्यनिष्ठा means doing one's duty faithfully in all conditions, honestly and without craving reward. The watchman who guards his post through storm and cold, and who serves for the sake of duty rather than for praise or gain, shows the ideal of the कर्मयोगी. True greatness lies not in the reward we receive but in the sincerity with which we do what we ought.

चत्वारः श्लोकाः — Four verses on कर्म and कर्तव्य (with शब्दार्थ)

1) कर्मण्येवाधिकारस्ते मा फलेषु कदाचन ।
   मा कर्मफलहेतुर्भूर्मा ते सङ्गोऽस्त्वकर्मणि ॥ (श्रीमद्भगवद्गीता 2.47)
   शब्दार्थ: कर्मणि = in action/work; एव = alone, only; अधिकारः = right, entitlement; ते = your; मा = never, do not; फलेषु = in the fruits/results; कदाचन = ever, at any time; कर्मफलहेतुः = the cause of the fruit of action; मा भूः = do not be; ते = your; सङ्गः = attachment; मा अस्तु = let there not be; अकर्मणि = in inaction.
   Translation: You have a right only to your action, never to its fruits. Do not let the fruit of action be your motive, nor let your attachment be to inaction.
   Theme / Moral: The heart of कर्तव्यनिष्ठा — give your whole effort to the duty, but do not be enslaved by craving for its reward, and never use 'no reward' as an excuse for doing nothing.

2) उद्यमेन हि सिध्यन्ति कार्याणि न मनोरथैः ।
   न हि सुप्तस्य सिंहस्य प्रविशन्ति मुखे मृगाः ॥
   शब्दार्थ: उद्यमेन = by effort; हि = indeed; सिध्यन्ति = are accomplished; कार्याणि = tasks, works; न = not; मनोरथैः = by (mere) wishes; सुप्तस्य = of the sleeping; सिंहस्य = of the lion; प्रविशन्ति = enter; मुखे = into the mouth; मृगाः = deer, animals.
   Translation: Tasks are accomplished by effort, not by mere wishes; deer do not walk into the mouth of a sleeping lion.
   Theme / Moral: कर्तव्यनिष्ठा requires actual effort (उद्यम), not day-dreaming. Even the mighty must work to obtain their aim.

3) स्वे स्वे कर्मण्यभिरतः संसिद्धिं लभते नरः ।
   स्वकर्मनिरतः सिद्धिं यथा विन्दति तच्छृणु ॥ (श्रीमद्भगवद्गीता 18.45)
   शब्दार्थ: स्वे स्वे कर्मणि = each in his own work/duty; अभिरतः = devoted, engaged; संसिद्धिम् = perfection, full success; लभते = attains; नरः = a person; स्वकर्मनिरतः = intent on one's own duty; सिद्धिम् = success/perfection; यथा = how, in what way; विन्दति = obtains; तत् शृणु = hear that.
   Translation: Devoted each to his own duty, a person attains perfection. Hear now how one intent on his own work finds that perfection.
   Theme / Moral: One reaches the highest success not by envying another's role but by doing one's own duty (स्वकर्म) wholeheartedly.

4) श्रेयान्स्वधर्मो विगुणः परधर्मात्स्वनुष्ठितात् ।
   स्वधर्मे निधनं श्रेयः परधर्मो भयावहः ॥ (श्रीमद्भगवद्गीता 3.35)
   शब्दार्थ: श्रेयान् = better; स्वधर्मः = one's own duty; विगुणः = imperfect, deficient; परधर्मात् = than another's duty; स्वनुष्ठितात् = (though) well performed; स्वधर्मे = in one's own duty; निधनम् = death; श्रेयः = better; परधर्मः = another's duty; भयावहः = fraught with fear, dangerous.
   Translation: Better is one's own duty though imperfect than another's duty well performed. Better is death in one's own duty; another's duty brings fear.
   Theme / Moral: Be true to your own कर्तव्य. Doing your own duty, even with faults, is nobler than abandoning it to imitate another's.

व्याकरणम् — A little grammar from the lesson (English explanation, Devanagari examples)

(A) सन्धि (Sandhi — joining of sounds).
  • यण्-सन्धि: when इ/उ etc. meet a dissimilar vowel, they become य्/व्. कर्मणि + एव = कर्मण्येव (इ + ए → य् + ए). Split back (सन्धि-विच्छेद) as कर्मणि + एव.
  • दीर्घ-सन्धि: a short vowel + a similar vowel → one long vowel. न + अस्ति = नास्ति (अ + अ = आ); तथा + अपि = तथापि.
  • गुण/वृद्धि: सु + अनुष्ठितात् = स्वनुष्ठितात् (उ + अ → व); कर्मणि + अधिकारः → कर्मण्यधिकारः.
  • विसर्ग-सन्धि: सङ्गः + अस्तु → सङ्गोऽस्तु (visarga + अ → ओ, with अवग्रह ऽ). Being able to SPLIT a sandhi is a key reading skill.

(B) विभक्ति (Vibhakti — case endings). Using the masculine a-stem नर (man) as a model:
  • प्रथमा (nominative, subject): नरः — 'the man'. In the lesson नरः, प्रहरी, राजा.
  • द्वितीया (accusative, object): नरम् — the thing acted on. रक्षणम्, कर्तव्यम्, विश्रामम् are objects.
  • तृतीया (instrumental, 'by/with'): नरेण — the means. उद्यमेन 'by effort', रत्नैः 'with jewels', विनयेन 'humbly'.
  • चतुर्थी (dative, 'for'): नराय — purpose. पुरस्काराय 'for reward', सुखाय 'for comfort'.
  • पञ्चमी (ablative, 'from/than'): नरात् — source/comparison. परधर्मात् 'than another's duty', कर्तव्यात् 'than duty'.
  • षष्ठी (genitive, 'of'): नरस्य — possession. सुप्तस्य सिंहस्य 'of the sleeping lion', राजभवनस्य 'of the palace'.
  • सप्तमी (locative, 'in/at/on'): नरे — place/time. कर्मणि 'in action', फलेषु 'in the fruits', निशायाम् 'at night', नगरे 'in the city'.

(C) शब्दरूप (declension of the a-stem noun नर, masculine):
  प्रथमा: नरः (one), नरौ (two), नराः (many).
  द्वितीया: नरम्, नरौ, नरान्.
  तृतीया: नरेण, नराभ्याम्, नरैः.
  In the lesson जनाः (people) and चोराः (thieves) are प्रथमा बहुवचन (nominative plural), while प्रहरी (watchman) is singular.

(D) धातुरूप (conjugation, लट् लकार / present tense):
  • भू (to be/become), परस्मैपद: भवति / भवतः / भवन्ति; भवसि / भवथः / भवथ; भवामि / भवावः / भवामः.
  • कृ (to do), परस्मैपद: करोति / कुरुतः / कुर्वन्ति; करोषि / कुरुथः / कुरुथ; करोमि / कुर्वः / कुर्मः.
  In the story तिष्ठति (stands), करोमि (I do), न करोमि (I do not do) are all लट् लकार forms.

SUMMARY (सारांश)

In this chapter you learned that कर्तव्यनिष्ठा (कर्तव्यम् + निष्ठा) means steadfast, honest devotion to one's duty, done sincerely and without craving reward — the essence of कर्मयोग. Through the story of the dutiful watchman Dharmapala, who guarded the palace gate through storm and cold and served for duty's sake rather than for gain, you saw कर्तव्यनिष्ठा in action, and studied its शब्दार्थ, translation and moral. You then read four famous public-domain verses — कर्मण्येवाधिकारस्ते (a right to action, not to its fruit), उद्यमेन हि सिध्यन्ति कार्याणि (effort, not wishing, brings success), स्वे स्वे कर्मण्यभिरतः (perfection through one's own duty), and श्रेयान्स्वधर्मः (one's own duty is best) — each with word meanings and morals. Finally you drew grammar from the lesson: सन्धि (यण्, दीर्घ, विसर्ग) with सन्धि-विच्छेद, the seven विभक्ति case-endings with examples, the शब्दरूप of नर, and धातुरूप of भू and कृ. Remember: कर्मण्येवाधिकारस्ते — do your duty with your whole heart, and let the reward take care of itself.

sections.heading: What कर्तव्यनिष्ठा is and why it matters
bullets: कर्तव्यनिष्ठा = कर्तव्यम् (duty, what ought to be done) + निष्ठा (firm devotion): sincere, steadfast devotion to one's duty.
It is the essence of कर्मयोग — giving full effort to the duty itself while not being enslaved by craving for its fruit.
A person of कर्तव्यनिष्ठा becomes trustworthy (विश्वसनीयः), respected (माननीयः) and inwardly peaceful; society runs well only when each does his own duty.

sections.heading: The story of the dutiful watchman
bullets: धर्मपालः, the palace gatekeeper, stood alert at the gate every night.
During a terrible storm he refused to leave his post, thinking 'there is nothing greater than duty' (कर्तव्यात् महत्तरम् अन्यत् न अस्ति).
The king came in disguise; the watchman said he served neither for comfort nor reward but for duty's sake.
The king honoured him and called him a true कर्मयोगी — one who does his duty without looking to its fruit.

sections.heading: Verses on कर्म and duty
bullets: कर्मण्येवाधिकारस्ते मा फलेषु कदाचन (Gita 2.47): you have a right to action, never to its fruits.
उद्यमेन हि सिध्यन्ति कार्याणि न मनोरथैः: tasks are achieved by effort, not by mere wishes.
स्वे स्वे कर्मण्यभिरतः संसिद्धिं लभते नरः (Gita 18.45): devoted to one's own duty, a person attains perfection.
श्रेयान्स्वधर्मो विगुणः परधर्मात्स्वनुष्ठितात् (Gita 3.35): one's own duty, though imperfect, is better than another's well done.

sections.heading: Moral and ethical themes
bullets: Honesty (सत्यम्): being truthful about what our duty is and doing it sincerely.
Responsibility (उत्तरदायित्वम्): owning the results of doing — or failing to do — our duty.
Non-attachment to reward: work with full effort but without greed or fear about the outcome.
स्वधर्म: be true to your own duty rather than envying or imitating another's role.

sections.heading: Grammar from the lesson
bullets: सन्धि: यण् — कर्मणि + एव = कर्मण्येव; दीर्घ — न + अस्ति = नास्ति, तथा + अपि = तथापि; विसर्ग — सङ्गः + अस्तु = सङ्गोऽस्तु; splitting back is सन्धि-विच्छेद.
विभक्ति: कर्मणि/फलेषु/निशायाम् (सप्तमी 'in/at'), उद्यमेन/रत्नैः (तृतीया 'by/with'), पुरस्काराय (चतुर्थी 'for'), परधर्मात् (पञ्चमी 'than/from'), सिंहस्य (षष्ठी 'of').
शब्दरूप of a-stem नर: प्रथमा नरः/नरौ/नराः; द्वितीया नरम्/नरौ/नरान्.

key_takeaways: कर्तव्यनिष्ठा (कर्तव्यम् + निष्ठा) is steadfast, honest devotion to one's duty, done without craving reward.
कर्मण्येवाधिकारस्ते मा फलेषु कदाचन — you have a right to your action, never to its fruits.
The watchman धर्मपालः shows कर्तव्यनिष्ठा by guarding his post through storm and serving for duty, not gain.
उद्यमेन हि सिध्यन्ति कार्याणि न मनोरथैः — effort, not wishing, accomplishes tasks.
श्रेयान्स्वधर्मः — one's own duty, even if imperfect, is better than another's well performed.
Honesty (सत्यम्) and responsibility (उत्तरदायित्वम्) are the two wings of कर्तव्यनिष्ठा.
विभक्ति endings show a word's role: तृतीया 'by', चतुर्थी 'for', पञ्चमी 'than/from', षष्ठी 'of', सप्तमी 'in'.

glossary.definition: Steadfast devotion to one's duty (कर्तव्यम् + निष्ठा): doing sincerely and honestly what one ought to do, without craving reward.
That which ought to be done; one's duty or responsibility.
Firm devotion, steadfastness, dedication to something.
The yoga of action — doing one's duty with full effort as an offering, without attachment to its fruit.
One who practises कर्मयोग; a person who does his duty without craving its reward, like the watchman धर्मपालः.
A watchman or sentinel; in the story the gatekeeper (द्वारपालः) of the royal palace.
Right or entitlement; in Gita 2.47 one has अधिकार only to action, not to its fruit.
Fruit, result or reward of an action; the कर्मयोगी works without desiring फल.
Effort, industry, diligence; by उद्यम tasks are accomplished (उद्यमेन हि सिध्यन्ति कार्याणि).
One's own duty or role; श्रेयान्स्वधर्मः — one's own duty is better than another's.
Responsibility; owning the results of doing or not doing one's duty.
The joining/merging of sounds where words meet; e.g. यण्-सन्धि कर्मणि + एव = कर्मण्येव.
A noun's case ending showing its role: प्रथमा subject, तृतीया 'by', चतुर्थी 'for', पञ्चमी 'from/than', षष्ठी 'of', सप्तमी 'in'.
The full declension of a noun through cases and numbers, e.g. नर: नरः / नरौ / नराः in the nominative.
The conjugation of a verb-root through persons and numbers, e.g. भू → भवति; कृ → करोति in लट् लकार (present).

worksheet.title: Worksheet — कर्तव्यनिष्ठा (NIOS Sanskrit 209, Chapter 18)
worksheet.instructions: Attempt all questions. Write Sanskrit words in Devanagari and give your explanations in English. Refer to the story and verses in the lesson where needed.

questions.question: What does the word कर्तव्यनिष्ठा mean, and of which two words is it made?
questions.answer: कर्तव्यनिष्ठा means steadfast, sincere devotion to one's duty. It is made of कर्तव्यम् (that which ought to be done, one's duty) + निष्ठा (firm devotion, steadfastness).
questions.explanation: Definition plus the compound कर्तव्यम् + निष्ठा.

questions.question:
Translate into simple English:
कर्मण्येवाधिकारस्ते मा फलेषु कदाचन ।
मा कर्मफलहेतुर्भूर्मा ते सङ्गोऽस्त्वकर्मणि ॥
questions.answer: You have a right only to your action (कर्म), never to its fruits (फल). Do not let the fruit of action be your motive, and let not your attachment be to inaction (अकर्म).
questions.explanation: Gita 2.47 — the cardinal verse of कर्तव्यनिष्ठा: full effort, no craving for reward, and no excuse for inaction.

questions.question: Give the शब्दार्थ (English word meaning) of each: प्रहरी, कर्तव्यम्, रक्षणम्, फलम्, उद्यमः.
questions.answer: प्रहरी = watchman/sentinel; कर्तव्यम् = duty (what ought to be done); रक्षणम् = protection/guarding; फलम् = fruit/reward/result; उद्यमः = effort/industry.
questions.explanation: Core vocabulary from the story and verses.

questions.question: Why did the watchman धर्मपालः refuse to leave his post during the storm? Answer in one or two sentences.
questions.answer: Because he believed guarding the palace was his duty and that if he left, thieves might enter. He thought there is nothing greater than duty (कर्तव्यात् महत्तरम् अन्यत् न अस्ति), so he stayed alert through the rain and cold.
questions.explanation: Shows कर्तव्यनिष्ठा — duty above comfort.

questions.question: Do the सन्धि-विच्छेद (split) of: (a) कर्मण्येव (b) नास्ति.
questions.answer: (a) कर्मण्येव = कर्मणि + एव (इ + ए → य् + ए, यण्-सन्धि). (b) नास्ति = न + अस्ति (अ + अ = आ, दीर्घ-सन्धि).
questions.explanation: Splitting a joined form back into its words is सन्धि-विच्छेद.

questions.question: State the विभक्ति (case) and its meaning-role of each: उद्यमेन, पुरस्काराय, परधर्मात्.
questions.answer: उद्यमेन = तृतीया (instrumental) → 'by effort'. पुरस्काराय = चतुर्थी (dative) → 'for reward'. परधर्मात् = पञ्चमी (ablative) → 'than/from another's duty'.
questions.explanation: तृतीया shows means, चतुर्थी shows purpose, पञ्चमी shows source/comparison.

questions.question: Explain the idea of कर्मयोग using the verse 'कर्मण्येवाधिकारस्ते मा फलेषु कदाचन'. How can a student practise this idea while studying?
questions.answer:
The verse teaches that we have a right (अधिकार) only to our action (कर्म), never to its fruits (फल). We should not make the reward our sole motive, nor use 'I may not get a reward' as an excuse for doing nothing (अकर्म). This is कर्मयोग: giving our full effort to the duty itself, calmly and honestly, while leaving the result to take care of itself. It does not mean results do not matter; it means we should not be paralysed by greed for success or fear of failure.
A student can practise this by studying sincerely and regularly for the sake of learning and duty, not only for marks; by not cheating or cutting corners to grab a reward; by doing homework and helping in class without expecting praise; and by staying steady and calm about exam results, focusing on effort. This builds concentration, honesty and peace of mind.
questions.explanation: Explain अधिकार over कर्म not फल; non-attachment; avoid अकर्म; then practical study applications.

questions.question: Write three simple Sanskrit sentences (in Devanagari) about doing one's duty (कर्तव्यम्), and give their English meaning.
questions.answer:
1. छात्रः प्रतिदिनं स्वकर्तव्यं करोति। (The student does his duty every day.)
2. प्रहरी द्वारे सावधानः तिष्ठति। (The watchman stands alert at the gate.)
3. वयं फलम् अनपेक्ष्य कर्म कुर्मः। (We do our work without expecting reward.)
Together they say: we should do our duty daily, remain alert and responsible, and work without craving reward.
questions.explanation: Simple प्रथमा-subject sentences using लट् forms करोति, तिष्ठति, कुर्मः and chapter vocabulary.

questions.question: What is the moral (सारः) of the story of the dutiful watchman?
questions.answer: The moral is कर्तव्यनिष्ठा: one should do one's duty faithfully in all conditions, honestly and without craving reward. True greatness lies not in the reward received but in the sincerity with which we do what we ought — the ideal of the कर्मयोगी.
questions.explanation: Duty done sincerely and selflessly is the mark of a true कर्मयोगी.

questions.question: Translate and give the moral of: 'श्रेयान्स्वधर्मो विगुणः परधर्मात्स्वनुष्ठितात्'.
questions.answer: Translation: Better is one's own duty (स्वधर्म), though imperfect (विगुण), than another's duty (परधर्म) well performed. Moral: We should be true to our own duty rather than abandon it to imitate someone else's role; doing our own कर्तव्य sincerely is nobler than copying another's.
questions.explanation: Gita 3.35 — the value of स्वधर्म over परधर्म.

questions.question: What does कर्तव्यनिष्ठा mean? Answer in one sentence.
questions.answer: कर्तव्यनिष्ठा means steadfast, sincere devotion to one's duty — doing honestly and completely what one ought to do, without craving reward.
questions.explanation: कर्तव्यम् (duty) + निष्ठा (devotion).

questions.question: What is कर्मयोग, and how does it relate to कर्तव्यनिष्ठा?
questions.answer: कर्मयोग is doing one's duty with full effort as an offering, without attachment to its fruit. It is the very essence of कर्तव्यनिष्ठा: we give our whole effort to the duty itself and do not crave reward.
questions.explanation: Effort in action + non-attachment to result = कर्मयोग.

questions.question: Who was धर्मपालः and what was his duty?
questions.answer: धर्मपालः was the watchman (प्रहरी) and gatekeeper (द्वारपालः) of the royal palace. His duty was to guard the palace gate, standing alert every night.
questions.explanation: He guarded the राजभवन at night.

questions.question: Describe what happened when the king came to the gate at night.
questions.answer: The king came in disguise (गुप्तवेषेण) during a storm and asked the watchman why he stood there in the rain and cold, telling him to go home and rest. धर्मपालः humbly replied that it was his duty, and that he stood there neither for comfort nor for reward but for duty's sake. The king was greatly pleased.
questions.explanation: Tests the watchman's कर्तव्यनिष्ठा through the king's disguise.

questions.question: Why did the king call धर्मपालः a true कर्मयोगी?
questions.answer: Because धर्मपालः did his duty faithfully without desiring any reward — 'he who does his own duty without looking to its fruit is blessed'. Such selfless, dutiful action is exactly कर्मयोग.
questions.explanation: यः फलम् अनपेक्ष्य स्वकर्तव्यं करोति, सः एव धन्यः.

questions.question: What qualities of character does धर्मपालः show in the story? Name at least three.
questions.answer: He shows (1) devotion to duty (कर्तव्यनिष्ठा) by staying at his post through the storm; (2) honesty and sincerity, guarding well even when unwatched; (3) humility (विनय/नम्रता) in his words to the king; and (4) selflessness, serving for duty rather than reward.
questions.explanation: Duty, honesty, humility and selflessness are all displayed.

questions.question: Give the शब्दार्थ of: वृष्टिः, वातः, रक्षणम्.
questions.answer: वृष्टिः = rain; वातः = wind; रक्षणम् = protection / guarding.
questions.explanation: Weather and duty vocabulary from the story.

questions.question: Give the शब्दार्थ of: अधिकारः, फलम्, अकर्मणि.
questions.answer: अधिकारः = right / entitlement; फलम् = fruit / reward / result; अकर्मणि = in inaction.
questions.explanation: Key words from कर्मण्येवाधिकारस्ते.

questions.question: Use the word 'कर्तव्यम्' in a simple Sanskrit sentence and give its English meaning.
questions.answer: Sentence: छात्रः स्वकर्तव्यं करोति। Meaning: The student does his duty. Here कर्तव्यम् means 'duty (what ought to be done)'.
questions.explanation: Uses कर्तव्यम् as the object (द्वितीया) of करोति.

questions.question: Explain the meaning of 'कर्मण्येवाधिकारस्ते मा फलेषु कदाचन'.
questions.answer: It means: you have a right only to your action (कर्म), never to its fruits (फल). We should do our duty with full effort but not make the reward our motive. This is the central teaching of कर्तव्यनिष्ठा and कर्मयोग.
questions.explanation: Right over action, not over its fruit.

questions.question: What does the verse 'उद्यमेन हि सिध्यन्ति कार्याणि न मनोरथैः' teach?
questions.answer: It teaches that tasks are accomplished by effort (उद्यम), not by mere wishes or day-dreams (मनोरथ). The image of deer not entering a sleeping lion's mouth shows that even the strong must make effort.
questions.explanation: Effort, not wishing, brings success.

questions.question: Compare the messages of 'कर्मण्येवाधिकारस्ते...' and 'उद्यमेन हि सिध्यन्ति...'. How do they together describe कर्तव्यनिष्ठा?
questions.answer: 'उद्यमेन हि सिध्यन्ति...' stresses the EFFORT side of duty — nothing is achieved without hard work. 'कर्मण्येवाधिकारस्ते...' stresses the NON-ATTACHMENT side — we must not crave the reward of that work. Together they describe कर्तव्यनिष्ठा perfectly: give full, sincere effort to your duty, yet remain unattached to its fruit.
questions.explanation: Effort + non-attachment = complete कर्तव्यनिष्ठा.

questions.question: Name two moral values taught by this lesson and explain each briefly.
questions.answer: (1) Honesty (सत्यम्): being truthful about our duty and doing it sincerely, even when unwatched. (2) Responsibility (उत्तरदायित्वम्): owning the results of doing or not doing our duty. Both are the wings of कर्तव्यनिष्ठा.
questions.explanation: Honesty and responsibility support devotion to duty.

questions.question: 'One should not desire reward, but one should still work hard.' Is this a contradiction? Explain.
questions.answer: No, it is not a contradiction. Non-attachment to reward concerns our MOTIVE and our peace of mind, not the quality of our work. We should give full, sincere effort to the duty itself, and simply not let greed for reward or fear of failure control us. In fact, freedom from anxiety about the result often improves the effort. This is exactly कर्मयोग.
questions.explanation: Effort and non-attachment operate on different levels — action vs. craving.

questions.question: Give two examples from daily life that show कर्तव्यनिष्ठा.
questions.answer: Examples: (1) a doctor or nurse who treats patients faithfully even at night or in difficulty; (2) a student who studies sincerely and does homework honestly without needing praise. Both do their duty faithfully and selflessly.
questions.explanation: Faithful, selfless duty in real roles mirrors the watchman.

questions.question: Translate into English: 'अहं फलम् इच्छन् कर्म न करोमि।'

questions.explanation: The watchman's statement of selfless action.

questions.question: Translate and briefly explain: 'स्वे स्वे कर्मण्यभिरतः संसिद्धिं लभते नरः।'
questions.answer: Translation: Devoted each to his own work/duty, a person attains perfection (संसिद्धि). Explanation: One reaches the highest success not by envying another's role but by doing one's own duty wholeheartedly — a key idea of कर्तव्यनिष्ठा.
questions.explanation: Gita 18.45 — perfection through devotion to one's own duty.

questions.question: Retell the story of the dutiful watchman धर्मपालः in your own words (in English) and state its moral.
questions.answer: In a certain city, धर्मपालः was the watchman and gatekeeper of the royal palace, standing guard alertly every night. One night a terrible storm broke, with heavy rain and strong wind, and everyone slept indoors. Yet धर्मपालः refused to leave his post, thinking that guarding the palace was his duty and that if he left, thieves might enter — 'there is nothing greater than duty'. That night the king came to the gate in disguise and, seeing him in the rain and cold, told him to go home and rest. धर्मपालः humbly replied that this was his duty, that doing his duty was his dharma, and that he stood there neither for comfort nor for reward. Greatly pleased, the king honoured him in the morning with jewels and wealth; but धर्मपालः modestly said he did not work desiring reward, for the work itself was his joy. The king then declared him a true कर्मयोगी. Moral: We should do our duty faithfully in all conditions, honestly and without craving reward; true greatness lies in the sincerity of our duty, not in the reward we receive.
questions.explanation: Full narrative plus the moral of selfless कर्तव्यनिष्ठा.

questions.question: 'कर्तव्यनिष्ठा is important for both the individual and society.' Discuss with reasons.
questions.answer: कर्तव्यनिष्ठा — sincere devotion to duty — benefits the individual because honest, faithful work brings self-respect, trust, and a clear conscience; a person who does his duty well becomes reliable (विश्वसनीयः) and inwardly peaceful, free from the anxiety and guilt that follow neglect. It benefits society because every role — student, farmer, soldier, teacher, doctor, parent — is a thread in the social fabric; when each person does his own duty faithfully, society runs smoothly and safely. When people neglect duty — a guard who abandons his post, a doctor who ignores a patient — the harm spreads far beyond themselves. The Gita's teaching कर्मण्येवाधिकारस्ते adds that we should do our duty for its own sake, not merely for reward, which keeps our motives honest. Thus कर्तव्यनिष्ठा links personal integrity with the common good, and is essential for a healthy individual life and a well-ordered society.
questions.explanation: Individual benefits (trust, peace) plus social benefits (smooth, safe society).

questions.question: Explain the four verses of this chapter and show how each contributes to the idea of कर्तव्यनिष्ठा.
questions.answer: (1) कर्मण्येवाधिकारस्ते (Gita 2.47): we have a right to action, never to its fruit — so we must work without craving reward. This gives कर्तव्यनिष्ठा its spirit of non-attachment. (2) उद्यमेन हि सिध्यन्ति कार्याणि: tasks are done by effort, not wishes — this supplies the effort side, showing that duty demands real work, not day-dreaming. (3) स्वे स्वे कर्मण्यभिरतः संसिद्धिं लभते नरः (Gita 18.45): one attains perfection by devotion to one's OWN duty — this shows the reward of faithful कर्तव्यनिष्ठा is inner perfection. (4) श्रेयान्स्वधर्मः (Gita 3.35): one's own duty, though imperfect, is better than another's well done — this teaches loyalty to one's own role rather than envy of others. Together the verses say: work hard at your own duty, without craving reward, and you will attain perfection — the complete teaching of कर्तव्यनिष्ठा.
questions.explanation: Each verse adds one pillar: non-attachment, effort, perfection, and स्वधर्म.

questions.question: How can a student apply the teaching of कर्तव्यनिष्ठा in school and at home? Give at least four practical ways.
questions.answer: A student can apply कर्तव्यनिष्ठा by: (1) studying sincerely and regularly for the sake of learning and duty, not only for marks or prizes; (2) doing homework and classwork honestly, without copying or cutting corners, even when no one is watching; (3) fulfilling responsibilities at home — helping parents, caring for younger siblings, keeping promises — as a duty, not for reward; (4) staying calm and steady about exam results, focusing on effort rather than being anxious about the outcome (कर्मण्येवाधिकारस्ते); and (5) doing one's OWN duties well rather than envying others' roles (श्रेयान्स्वधर्मः). These habits build honesty, discipline, responsibility and peace of mind, turning the lesson's ideal into daily practice.
questions.explanation: Practical, reward-free, honest duty in study and home life.

questions.question: Write short notes with examples on (a) सन्धि and (b) विभक्ति as seen in this lesson.
questions.answer: (a) सन्धि (joining of sounds): When words meet, their sounds combine. Examples from the lesson — यण्-सन्धि: कर्मणि + एव = कर्मण्येव (इ + ए → य् + ए); दीर्घ-सन्धि: न + अस्ति = नास्ति, तथा + अपि = तथापि (a short vowel + a like vowel → one long vowel); विसर्ग-सन्धि: सङ्गः + अस्तु = सङ्गोऽस्तु. Splitting a joined form back (सन्धि-विच्छेद) is a key reading skill. (b) विभक्ति (case endings): A noun's ending shows its role. Examples — प्रथमा नरः/प्रहरी (subject); द्वितीया कर्तव्यम्/रक्षणम् (object); तृतीया उद्यमेन/रत्नैः ('by/with'); चतुर्थी पुरस्काराय ('for'); पञ्चमी परधर्मात् ('than/from'); षष्ठी सिंहस्य ('of'); सप्तमी कर्मणि/फलेषु/निशायाम् ('in/at'). Knowing the case tells us how each word works in the sentence.
questions.explanation: Covers types of सन्धि with examples and the seven विभक्ति with examples.

questions.question: Translate the following passage into simple English: 'एकस्मिन् नगरे धर्मपालः नाम प्रहरी आसीत्। सः राजभवनस्य द्वारपालः आसीत्। एकदा घोरा वृष्टिः अभवत्। तथापि सः स्वस्थानं न अत्यजत्। सः अचिन्तयत् — मम कर्तव्यं रक्षणम्।'
questions.answer: In a certain city there was a watchman named Dharmapala. He was the gatekeeper of the royal palace. One day a terrible rain fell. Yet he did not leave his post. He thought, 'My duty is protection (guarding the palace).'
questions.explanation: Sentence-by-sentence translation of the story's opening.

questions.question:
Read the passage and answer:
'एकदा घोरा वृष्टिः अभवत्, प्रबलः वातः च ववौ। तथापि धर्मपालः स्वस्थानं न अत्यजत्। सः अचिन्तयत् — मम कर्तव्यं राजभवनस्य रक्षणम्। यदि अहं स्थानं त्यजामि, तर्हि चोराः प्रविशेयुः।'
(a) What was the weather like? (b) What did धर्मपालः refuse to do? (c) Why? (d) Which value does this show?
questions.answer: (a) There was a terrible rain and a strong wind (घोरा वृष्टिः, प्रबलः वातः). (b) He refused to leave his post (स्वस्थानं न अत्यजत्). (c) Because guarding the palace was his duty, and if he left, thieves might enter (चोराः प्रविशेयुः). (d) It shows कर्तव्यनिष्ठा — devotion to duty above comfort.
questions.explanation: Comprehension of the storm scene and the value of duty.

questions.question:
Read the passage and answer:
'राजा स्वयं गुप्तवेषेण द्वारम् आगच्छत्। सः अपृच्छत् — भो प्रहरिन्, किमर्थं त्वम् एवं वृष्टौ तिष्ठसि? गृहं गच्छ। धर्मपालः अवदत् — देव, इदं मम कर्तव्यम्।'
(a) Who came to the gate and how? (b) What did he ask? (c) What did धर्मपालः reply? (d) Give the शब्दार्थ of किमर्थम्.
questions.answer: (a) The king himself came to the gate in disguise (गुप्तवेषेण). (b) He asked why the watchman was standing in the rain and told him to go home. (c) धर्मपालः replied, 'Sire, this is my duty' (इदं मम कर्तव्यम्). (d) किमर्थम् = 'why / for what purpose'.
questions.explanation: Comprehension of the king's test and the watchman's reply.

questions.question:
Read the verse and answer:
'कर्मण्येवाधिकारस्ते मा फलेषु कदाचन। मा कर्मफलहेतुर्भूर्मा ते सङ्गोऽस्त्वकर्मणि॥'
(a) To what do we have a right? (b) To what do we NOT have a right? (c) What are we warned not to be attached to? (d) Name the source of the verse.
questions.answer: (a) We have a right only to our action (कर्म). (b) We do NOT have a right to its fruits (फल). (c) We are warned not to be attached to inaction (अकर्म). (d) The verse is from the श्रीमद्भगवद्गीता (2.47).
questions.explanation: Analysis of the cardinal verse on कर्तव्यनिष्ठा.

questions.question:
Read the verse and answer:
'उद्यमेन हि सिध्यन्ति कार्याणि न मनोरथैः। न हि सुप्तस्य सिंहस्य प्रविशन्ति मुखे मृगाः॥'
(a) By what are tasks accomplished? (b) By what are they NOT accomplished? (c) What image is used? (d) What is its moral?
questions.answer: (a) Tasks are accomplished by effort (उद्यमेन). (b) They are NOT accomplished by mere wishes (मनोरथैः). (c) The image is of deer not entering the mouth of a sleeping lion. (d) Moral: even the strong must make effort; success comes from hard work, not day-dreaming.
questions.explanation: Comprehension and moral of the effort verse.

questions.question: Case: Ravi does his class-monitor duties well only when the teacher is watching, and neglects them otherwise. (a) Does Ravi show कर्तव्यनिष्ठा? (b) Why or why not? (c) What should he do instead? (d) Which verse supports your advice?
questions.answer: (a) No, Ravi does not truly show कर्तव्यनिष्ठा. (b) Because real devotion to duty means doing it sincerely even when no one is watching; working only to be seen is done for reward/praise, not for duty. (c) He should do his monitor duties honestly and consistently for their own sake, whether or not he is watched or praised. (d) कर्मण्येवाधिकारस्ते मा फलेषु कदाचन — do the duty, do not crave the reward.
questions.explanation: Applies the non-attachment and honesty themes to a real case.

questions.question: Case: During a flood, a young doctor keeps treating patients through the night though very tired and unpaid. (a) Which value does she show? (b) How is she like धर्मपालः? (c) Which Sanskrit word describes such a person? (d) Give one शब्दार्थ: निष्ठा.
questions.answer: (a) She shows कर्तव्यनिष्ठा — devotion to duty. (b) Like धर्मपालः, she stays at her post in hard conditions and serves without craving reward. (c) She is a कर्मयोगी (one devoted to selfless action). (d) निष्ठा = firm devotion / steadfastness.
questions.explanation: Connects a modern example to the watchman and to कर्मयोग.

questions.question:
Read and answer:
'धर्मपालः नम्रः सन् अवदत् — राजन्, अहं फलम् इच्छन् कर्म न करोमि। कर्म एव मम आनन्दः।'
(a) Translate the passage into English. (b) What does नम्रः mean? (c) What is धर्मपालः's attitude to reward? (d) Give the शब्दार्थ of आनन्दः.
questions.answer: (a) Translation: Being humble, धर्मपालः said, 'O king, I do not do work desiring (its) reward. The work itself is my joy.' (b) नम्रः = humble / modest. (c) He works without desiring reward; the duty itself gives him joy. (d) आनन्दः = joy / bliss.
questions.explanation: Translation plus comprehension of the watchman's selfless attitude.

questions.question: Grammar case. From the sentence 'सः उद्यमेन कर्मणि रक्षणम् करोति', answer: (a) case of उद्यमेन; (b) case of कर्मणि; (c) case of रक्षणम्; (d) the धातु (root) of करोति.
questions.answer: (a) उद्यमेन = तृतीया (instrumental, 'by effort'). (b) कर्मणि = सप्तमी (locative, 'in action'). (c) रक्षणम् = द्वितीया (accusative, the object 'protection'). (d) The root of करोति is कृ (to do).
questions.explanation: Identifies three cases and the verb root.

questions.question: Vocabulary case. Give the शब्दार्थ (English meaning) of each word from the lesson: (a) प्रहरी (b) कर्तव्यम् (c) स्वधर्मः (d) कर्मयोगी.
questions.answer: (a) प्रहरी = watchman / sentinel. (b) कर्तव्यम् = duty (what ought to be done). (c) स्वधर्मः = one's own duty. (d) कर्मयोगी = one devoted to selfless action.
questions.explanation: Recall of four key vocabulary items.

questions.question:
Read and answer:
'सत्यम् (honesty) and उत्तरदायित्वम् (responsibility) are the two wings of कर्तव्यनिष्ठा. We must be honest about what our duty is, and own the results of doing or not doing it.'
(a) What are the two wings of कर्तव्यनिष्ठा? (b) What does उत्तरदायित्वम् mean? (c) Why is honesty needed? (d) In one line, define कर्तव्यनिष्ठा.
questions.answer: (a) The two wings are honesty (सत्यम्) and responsibility (उत्तरदायित्वम्). (b) उत्तरदायित्वम् = responsibility — owning the results of doing or not doing one's duty. (c) Honesty is needed so we are truthful about what our duty really is and do it sincerely. (d) कर्तव्यनिष्ठा is steadfast, honest devotion to one's duty, done without craving reward.
questions.explanation: Comprehension of the meaning and moral basis of कर्तव्यनिष्ठा.

questions.question: Describe the watchman धर्मपालः — who he was, where he worked, and the main events of his story in order.
questions.answer: धर्मपालः was a watchman (प्रहरी) and gatekeeper (द्वारपालः) of the royal palace, who stood alert at the gate every night. The main events, in order: (1) One night a terrible rain fell and a strong wind blew, and everyone slept indoors. (2) धर्मपालः refused to leave his post, thinking that guarding the palace was his duty and that thieves might enter if he left. (3) The king himself came in disguise and asked why he stood in the rain, telling him to go home and rest. (4) धर्मपालः humbly replied that this was his duty and that he served neither for comfort nor for reward. (5) In the morning the king honoured him with jewels and wealth, but he modestly said the work itself was his joy. (6) The king declared him a true कर्मयोगी.
questions.explanation: Recall of the character and the ordered sequence of events.

questions.question: Give the शब्दार्थ (English word meaning) of at least eight Sanskrit words drawn from this lesson, and use any two of them in short Sanskrit sentences.
questions.answer:
शब्दार्थ: प्रहरी = watchman; द्वारपालः = gatekeeper; कर्तव्यम् = duty; रक्षणम् = protection; वृष्टिः = rain; चोरः = thief; अधिकारः = right; फलम् = reward/fruit; उद्यमः = effort; स्वधर्मः = one's own duty; कर्मयोगी = one devoted to selfless action.
Sentences: (1) प्रहरी द्वारे तिष्ठति। (The watchman stands at the gate.) (2) वयं फलम् अनपेक्ष्य कर्तव्यं कुर्मः। (We do our duty without expecting reward.)
questions.explanation: Vocabulary recall plus simple correct usage of two words.
